questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The food and being within Europe, since I didn't want to go too far in the case Covid broke out again.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: From KU's side it was alright, but from my host university it was a bit more difficult in regards to practicalities about the courses - such as schedule and exam dates. General info was fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The was an international office, but the opening hours are very limited and many people have questions. You could meet them on Teams or write them a mail, but the firth month they didn't respond to my mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It's Italy, so would recommend to have very low expectations in regards to planning, since nobody plans anything.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard. Bologna's housing market for students is insane. I ended up booking a room at something called TSH, but had to share it with another girl, and kitchen with approx. 300 others. I thought it was very expensive, thinking about that I didn't even have a room for myself. But it ended up being a really good experience, and I had a great roommate.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is not really any on campus options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Be aware that it is expensive and many people want to scam you. If you do not know anyone that has been in Bologna and has some contacts, then I would recommend going there early to search. Some of the people that started looking in beginning/mid September, first got accommodation in late October or had to move outside of Bologna and take the train/bus every morning. 
The local students says it has gotten even more crazy after Covid, since many apartments are now Airbnb instead of student housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy for most of my courses, but there was one course I couldn't sign up for due to an error on the webpage. I tried contacting 5 different people from my host university, and 1 responded 4 weeks after i send the mail. I ended up taking another course...

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up online

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Almost nothing. Your best shot is writing to the professor if you have any issues. It might be better later on in the semester, but you typically need the help in the beginning...

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, I couldn't register for one course, so I had to change that. And one course I changed one week into the semester, as I didn't like it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for preapproval to a lot of courses, so you can easily change if you can't sign up or you don't like the course. You can switch courses the first week or two, but you only have a course for 5 weeks, so you don't have much time if you change your mind.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally the academic level were a bit lower, but there was more work to do such as papers and presentations

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Overall kind of the same, but with less interaction between the professor and the students. And no breaks... I had 3 hours lectures and we only had a 10 minute break during those 3 hours

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, ADVANCED TOPICS IN LIQUIDITY MANAGEMENT
IN THE POST CRISIS ERA, FINANCIAL AND MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING, LAW AND ECONOMICS OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, FOUNDATIONS OF RISK REGULATION IN FINANCIAL MARKETS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Foundations of Risk Regulation in Financial Markets was really good I think, but also very difficult!

questions.answer: I spend more money on travelling around in Italy than expected. This is also why my personal spending is so high.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive. And beer, would recommend only to drink wine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was quite many different sports you could participate in, but you needed a medical approval to join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was quite many different sports you could participate in, but you needed a medical approval to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go for apertivo with you classmates!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy to travel to the larger cities in Italy (and cheap if you go by bus), so would recommend exploring other places than Bologna. Especially the southern part of Italy, since it is very different from Bologna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was alright

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: All the local students meet at Piazza Verdi for very cheap drinks almost every day of the week - go meet them there :-)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italian are never on time...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture about eating and taking the time to eat a nice dinner with friends and family

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Eat as much out as you can while you are there, you will miss it when you get back! And enjoy the cheap coffee

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of great new people!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing people at home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
